version.changelog: Clarify isolated Rocq theorem skill boundary

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, requirements, and scope are coherent with its stated purpose (setting up and running Rocq proofs); it is instruction-only, requests no credentials, and does not bundle or download code — but you should be cautious when building/running untrusted theorem workspaces because opam/dune builds can execute arbitrary code.

dimensions.detail: The skill name and description match the runtime instructions: it asks the agent to verify and use rocq (or coqc), dune, and opam to build and prove theorems. One minor metadata inconsistency: the registry summary lists 'Required binaries: none' while SKILL.md declares commands (rocq/coqc, dune, opam) as runtime requirements. This is likely an authoring omission in the registry metadata but worth noting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions stay on-task: they run local rocq/coqc, dune, opam, grep, and read local project files (README.md, .v files, dune/_CoqProject, opam). There are no external endpoints or secret exfiltration steps. Important security note: the workflow explicitly runs opam install and dune build in the project workspace — building or installing dependencies from an untrusted repository can execute arbitrary code (build hooks, scripts). The skill correctly warns about companion skills and not copying unseen directories into global skill locations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or remote download. Nothing is written to disk by the skill itself beyond the agent performing local commands in the existing workspace.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. It references opam switches and local toolchain state (appropriate for a build/prove workflow) but does not require secrets or unrelated service tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-included (always:false) and does not request persistent presence or modify other skills or global agent settings. It instructs running local commands only within the project workspace.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: guide and run local Rocq/Coq build and proof commands. Before using it, ensure the theorem workspace you will build comes from a trusted source — opam install and dune build can run arbitrary code from package hooks or build scripts. If you must run proofs on third-party projects, prefer running the workflow inside a sandbox/container or on an isolated VM, inspect the project's README/opam/dune files first, and avoid copying unknown companion skill directories into global agent skill folders. Also note the small metadata mismatch (registry says no required binaries while SKILL.md lists rocq/coqc, dune, and opam).
